window.placeholder: This window is a placeholder until its milestone ships.
send.permBody: Until you allow it, Glimpsfy only brings the app forward and you press ⌘V yourself.
send.copiedTemporary: The path was copied. History is off, so the file is deleted after 24 hours.
overlay.notReady: This action is not ready yet.
scroll.name: Scrolling capture
scroll.gap.above: A gap is left, so scroll up a little
scroll.gap.below: A gap is left, so scroll down a little
scroll.header: The sticky header is added once
scroll.footer: The bottom bar is added once
scroll.both: A sticky header and a bottom bar were found; each enters the result once, and the scrolled content goes between them
scroll.limit: {n} px are left before the limit
scroll.ended: The page ended; automatic scrolling stopped, and the result waits for Done

scroll.ax.title: Automatic scrolling needs Accessibility
scroll.ax.text: Glimpsfy sends scroll events to scroll the page for you, and macOS allows them only from apps with the Accessibility permission. Scrolling by hand works without it. Opening System Settings closes this capture.
scroll.noWindow: No window to scroll lies under the selection, so scroll it by hand.
scroll.empty: Nothing was captured yet, so scroll the page first.

overlay.size.tooBig: This size is larger than the screen, so the selection keeps its ratio at a smaller size.
overlay.size.window: While a window is captured, the window itself sets the size.
picker.blocked: This window is closed to capture.

agent.ask.area: asks for a screenshot of an area.
agent.ask.text: asks for the text in an area.

error.permission_denied: Glimpsfy needs the screen recording permission.
error.permission_denied@windows: Windows does not allow Glimpsfy to do this yet.
error.permission_denied@linux: The desktop did not let Glimpsfy share the screen.
error.not_implemented: This part of Glimpsfy is not ready yet.
error.io: The file could not be written.
error.not_found: The capture is no longer open.
error.not_confirmed: This host is not confirmed for uploads yet, so nothing was sent. Try again and confirm the host when Glimpsfy asks.

error.uploads_off: Uploads are turned off in Settings, so nothing was sent.
error.offline: Glimpsfy is offline, so it opened no connection.

error.keychain@linux: The desktop keyring refused access or is missing. Unlock it, or install GNOME Keyring or KWallet, and try again.
firstrun.title: Allow screen recording
firstrun.lead: Glimpsfy reads the screen only when you take a capture, and macOS asks you to allow that once.
firstrun.steps: Open System Settings, turn Glimpsfy on under Screen & System Audio Recording, and press the shortcut again.
firstrun.dev: A dev build asks on behalf of the app that started it, so macOS lists that app (often Terminal) instead of Glimpsfy.

annotate.snapUnavailable: Text recognition is unavailable, so the tool draws freely.
annotate.upload.noProvider: No upload host is set up yet. Choose one in Settings › Upload, which opens now, and then upload again.
annotate.upload.fix: {problem} Settings › Upload opens now so you can fix it.

upload.field.name: Name
upload.help.keychain: Glimpsfy keeps this key in the macOS keychain and never writes it into the settings file.
upload.help.keychain@windows: Glimpsfy keeps this key in the Windows Credential Manager and never writes it into the settings file.
upload.help.keychain@linux: Glimpsfy keeps this key in the desktop keyring and never writes it into the settings file.
upload.help.0x0.secret: 0x0.st then gives a longer link that is hard to guess. Anyone who has the link can still open the file.
upload.help.0x0.instance: Another server that runs the 0x0 software works too, and Glimpsfy asks again before its first upload.
upload.help.s3.endpoint: This is the address of the S3 service without the bucket, such as https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com or your MinIO server.
upload.help.s3.region: Every request is signed for this region. Most self-hosted servers accept us-east-1.
upload.help.s3.addressing: Automatic puts the bucket in the host name on Amazon S3 and in the path elsewhere. Most self-hosted servers need Path.
upload.help.s3.pathPrefix: Uploads go under this folder of the bucket. Glimpsfy fills in {date}, {year}, {month} and {day} at upload time.
upload.help.s3.publicUrl: When a CDN or another domain serves the bucket, Glimpsfy builds the link from this template. {key} is the uploaded file's key, and {bucket} is the bucket's name.
upload.help.s3.cacheControl: Glimpsfy sends this Cache-Control header with every upload, and the field may stay empty.
upload.help.custom.requestUrl: Only http and https addresses work. The host name is written out, and template calls may appear only in the path and the query.
upload.help.custom.fileFormName: This is the name of the form field that carries the image in a multipart body.
upload.help.custom.pairs: Glimpsfy keeps these values in the keychain, because they often hold tokens. The settings file keeps only the names.
upload.help.custom.pairs@windows: Glimpsfy keeps these values in the Credential Manager, because they often hold tokens. The settings file keeps only the names.
upload.help.custom.pairs@linux: Glimpsfy keeps these values in the keyring, because they often hold tokens. The settings file keeps only the names.
upload.help.custom.urlTemplate: Glimpsfy reads the link from the server's answer with {json:path}, {regex:pattern|group}, {header:name} or {response}.
upload.help.custom.deletionUrlTemplate: Glimpsfy reads the deletion link the same way and opens it in the browser when you delete the upload. The field may stay empty.
upload.help.custom.errorTemplate: Glimpsfy reads the server's reason from a refusal this way and shows it when an upload fails. The field may stay empty.
upload.host.catbox.operator: Catbox LLC runs catbox.moe and asks for its approval before any commercial use.
upload.host.litterbox.operator: Litterbox is Catbox's service for temporary files, and it stores your IP address with each upload.
upload.host.0x0.operator: 0x0.st describes itself as a public file host that one private person runs in Germany, and it stores your IP address and Glimpsfy's name with each file.
upload.host.imgbb.operator: ImgBB runs imgbb.com, and its terms name no company behind it.
upload.rule.maxLength: This value can be at most {max} characters long.
upload.rule.httpUrl: Enter an address that starts with https:// or http://.
upload.rule.noWhitespace: This value cannot contain spaces, so remove them.
upload.issue.required: This setting is required, so fill it in before you upload.
upload.issue.httpOnly: Only http and https addresses work here. Enter an address that starts with https://.
upload.issue.plainHttp: This address uses plain http, so the image and every key travel unencrypted. Use https unless the server is on your own network.
upload.issue.endpointQuery: The endpoint cannot carry a query, so remove everything from the question mark on.
upload.issue.bucketName: A bucket name has no slashes or spaces. Copy the name from your storage console.
upload.issue.dottedBucket: A bucket name with dots does not match Amazon's certificate when the bucket is in the host name. Choose Path addressing or a name without dots.
upload.issue.oneLine: This value must fit on one line, so remove the line breaks.
upload.issue.templateHost: The host name of the request URL must be written out. Template calls may appear only in the path and the query.
upload.issue.staticLink: This link never reads the server's answer, so every upload would get the same link. Add {json:…}, {regex:…}, {header:…} or {response}.
upload.issue.headerName: “{name}” is not a valid header name. A header name uses letters, digits and hyphens.
upload.issue.testFileKept: The test file {key} stayed in the bucket, because deleting it failed. Delete it in your storage console and check that the key may delete objects.
upload.syntax.unbalanced: A brace is missing. Every template call starts with { and ends with }.
upload.syntax.responseOnly: This call reads the server's answer, which does not exist yet while the request is sent. Use it only in the link, deletion link and error message.
upload.syntax.missingArgument: A template call is missing its argument. Write it as {json:path} or {regex:pattern|group}.
upload.syntax.nested: A call cannot hold another call here, so write the value out.
upload.syntax.otherInput: This call reads something other than the server's answer, which Glimpsfy does not do. Give {json:…} and {regex:…} only their own arguments.
upload.syntax.xml: Glimpsfy does not read XML answers. Read the value with {regex:pattern|group} instead.
upload.syntax.interactive: Calls like select, inputbox, outputbox and prompt ask a question during the upload, and Glimpsfy never does. Remove them from the template.
upload.syntax.input: The input call reads text you would type at upload time, which Glimpsfy does not support. Remove it from the template.
upload.syntax.unknown: Glimpsfy does not know this template call. The calls it reads are filename, random, base64, response, responseurl, header, json and regex.
upload.syntax.patternTooLong: The regular expression is longer than 1,000 characters, so shorten it.
upload.syntax.badPattern: The regular expression cannot be read. Check its brackets and its escapes.
upload.syntax.badJsonPath: The JSON path cannot be read. Write it like data.link or files[0].url.
upload.syntax.tooDeep: The template nests calls more than 16 deep, so write it with fewer calls inside one another.
upload.sxcu.tooLarge: The file is larger than 256 KB, which no custom uploader needs. Check that you picked the right file.
upload.sxcu.notJson: This is not a ShareX custom uploader file. Pick a .sxcu file.
upload.sxcu.legacyRegex: This file comes from an old ShareX version that numbers its patterns. Open it in a current ShareX, save it again and import the new file.
upload.sxcu.destination: This file uploads something other than images or files. Pick a ShareX file made for image or file uploads.
upload.sxcu.method: Only POST, PUT and PATCH requests carry a file, so choose one of them.
upload.sxcu.body: The file sends neither a multipart form nor the file alone, so it cannot carry a capture.
upload.sxcu.fileFormName: A multipart body needs the name of its file field. Enter the name the server expects.
upload.sxcu.reservedHeader: Glimpsfy sets the Host, Content-Length, Content-Type, Transfer-Encoding and Connection headers itself. Remove that header from the file.
upload.sxcu.pairValue: A parameter, header or argument has a value that is not text. Edit the file so that every value is text.
upload.sxcu.imported: Glimpsfy imported {name}. Its header, parameter and argument values are in the keychain now.
upload.sxcu.imported@windows: Glimpsfy imported {name}. Its header, parameter and argument values are in the Credential Manager now.
upload.sxcu.imported@linux: Glimpsfy imported {name}. Its header, parameter and argument values are in the keyring now.
upload.consent.title: Upload this capture to {name}?
upload.consent.destinationBucket: The image goes to the bucket {bucket} at {domain}.
upload.consent.testImage: Glimpsfy sends a 1 × 1 pixel test image to {domain}.
upload.consent.testBucket: Glimpsfy writes a small text file to the bucket {bucket} at {domain} and deletes it again.
upload.consent.testFrontPage: Glimpsfy opens the front page of {domain} to check that it answers.
upload.consent.visibility.anyoneWithLink: Anyone who has the link can open it.
upload.consent.visibility.bucketPolicy: The bucket's own access policy decides who can open it.
upload.consent.visibility.serverOwner: The server's owner decides who can open it.
upload.consent.visibility.notStated: {name} does not say who can open it.
upload.consent.retention.bySize: {name} keeps it for {minDays} to {maxDays} days, and smaller files stay longer.
upload.consent.retention.untilUnvisited: {name} keeps it until nobody has opened it for {period}.
upload.consent.retention.noExpiry: {name} states no expiry, so it stays until the host removes it.
upload.consent.retention.ownStorage: It stays until you delete it from your own storage.
upload.consent.retention.notStated: {name} does not say how long it keeps the file.
upload.consent.plainHttp: The connection is not encrypted, so anyone on the network path can read the image.
upload.consent.note: Glimpsfy asks this only once for each host.
upload.consent.noteAddress: Glimpsfy asks again if you change the address.
upload.consent.changed: The host's address changed while this dialog was open. Review the new address and confirm again.
upload.terms.visibility.anyoneWithLink: Anyone who has the link can open the file.
upload.terms.visibility.bucketPolicy: The bucket's own access policy decides who can open a file.
upload.terms.visibility.serverOwner: The server's owner decides who can open a file.
upload.terms.visibility.notStated: {name} does not say who can open a file.
upload.terms.retention.bySize: {name} keeps a file for {minDays} to {maxDays} days, and smaller files stay longer.
upload.terms.retention.inactivity: {name} removes a file after {period} without a visit.
upload.terms.retention.noExpiry: {name} states no expiry, so a file stays until the host removes it.
upload.terms.retention.ownStorage: A file stays until you delete it from your own storage.
upload.terms.retention.notStated: {name} does not say how long it keeps a file.
upload.terms.retention.chosen: {name} deletes each file after the time you choose below.
upload.terms.retention.optional: {name} deletes a file after the time you choose below, and with Never its terms do not say how long it stays.
upload.terms.deletion.none: Glimpsfy cannot delete an upload from {name}, so it stays until the host removes it.
upload.terms.deletion.request: Glimpsfy keeps the deletion token, so History can delete the file.
upload.terms.deletion.page: {name} returns a deletion page, which History opens when you delete from the host.
upload.state.copiedLink: The link is on the clipboard.
upload.state.copiedMarkdown: The Markdown image is on the clipboard.
upload.state.opened: The link opened in the browser.
upload.failed.cancelled: You cancelled the upload before the host returned a link.
upload.failed.provider: {name} refused the upload, and its reason is below.
upload.failed.providerStatus: {name} refused the upload with status {status}, and its reason is below.
upload.failed.network: Glimpsfy could not reach {name}. Check your connection and try again.
upload.failed.fileTooLarge: The file is larger than {name} accepts. Choose a smaller capture or another host.
upload.failed.hostNotAllowed: {name} tried to send the upload to another address, so Glimpsfy stopped it.
upload.failed.notConfirmed: Uploads to {name} are not confirmed yet. Upload again and confirm the host first.
upload.failed.missingSecret: {name} needs a key that is not stored yet. Add it in Settings › Upload.
upload.failed.invalidConfig: A setting of {name} is not valid. Fix it in Settings › Upload.
upload.failed.keychain: The keychain refused access. Unlock it and try again.
upload.failed.keychain@windows: Windows Credential Manager refused access. Try again, and restart Glimpsfy if it keeps refusing.
upload.failed.keychain@linux: The desktop keyring refused access or is missing. Unlock it, or install GNOME Keyring or KWallet, and try again.
upload.failed.io: Glimpsfy could not read the file. Check that it still exists.
upload.failed.uploadsOff: Uploads are turned off in Settings, so nothing was sent to {name}.
upload.failed.offline: Glimpsfy is offline, so nothing was sent to {name}.
upload.failed.other: The upload failed. Try again in a moment.
upload.failed.noProvider: No upload host is chosen yet. Choose one in Settings › Upload.
upload.delete.page: {name} deletes uploads on its own page, which is open in the browser now. The entry keeps its link until you delete the upload there.

history.foot.removed: Captures older than {days} days are removed, except pinned ones.
history.foot.forever: Captures stay until you delete them.
history.foot.off: New captures are not recorded while history is off.
history.sort.name: Name
history.off.title: History is off.
history.off.existing: New captures are not recorded, and the ones already here stay until you delete them or clear the history.
history.off.emptyText: New captures still go to the clipboard and to your folders, but no record of them is kept.
history.error.title: The history cannot be opened
history.error.text: Glimpsfy could not read its history ({reason}). Your captures and the files you saved are untouched.
history.empty.first.title: No captures yet
history.empty.first.text: Your first capture shows up here after you press {keys} and drag.
history.empty.first.textNoKeys: Your first capture shows up here after you capture an area from the menu bar.
history.empty.first.textNoKeys@windows: Your first capture shows up here after you capture an area from Glimpsfy’s icon in the notification area.
history.empty.first.textNoKeys@linux: Your first capture shows up here after you capture an area from the menu of Glimpsfy’s tray icon.
history.empty.noResults.title: Nothing matches “{query}”
history.empty.noResults.text: Search reads the text inside screenshots and their names, while recordings are skipped.
history.empty.filter.title: Nothing in {filter} yet
history.empty.filter.screenshots: Your screenshots show up here as soon as you take one.
history.empty.filter.recordings: Your screen recordings show up here when you stop them.
history.empty.filter.textCopies: Text you copy from the screen shows up here.
history.empty.filter.uploaded: Captures you upload show up here with their links.
history.empty.filter.pinned: Pinned captures stay here until you remove them, whatever the retention rule says.
history.empty.filter.app: No capture from this app is left in the history.
history.feed.label: Captures
history.series.revealFolder@linux: Show folder in the file manager
history.series.revealFrame@windows: Show this frame in File Explorer
history.series.revealFrame@linux: Show this frame in its folder
history.series.exporting: The timelapse is being written, and a note says when it is saved.
history.series.deleteLead: “{name}” leaves the history together with its folder of frames.
history.series.deleteSummary: The series leaves the history, and its folder of frames waits in the Trash until it is emptied.
history.series.deleteSummary@windows: The series leaves the history, and its folder of frames waits in the Recycle Bin until it is emptied.
history.series.deleteSummary@linux: The series leaves the history, and its folder of frames waits in the trash until it is emptied.
history.series.deleteSummaryMany: The folders of {n} series go to the Trash with their frames and wait there until it is emptied.
history.series.deleteSummaryMany@windows: The folders of {n} series go to the Recycle Bin with their frames and wait there until it is emptied.
history.series.deleteSummaryMany@linux: The folders of {n} series go to the trash with their frames and wait there until it is emptied.
history.mark.pinned: Pinned, kept until you remove it
history.bulk.label: Selection
history.bulk.combineOff: Select at least two screenshots to combine
history.combine.title: Combine {n} captures
history.combine.text: The result opens in the editor as a new image, and the captures you picked stay as they are.
history.combine.upscaled: {name} is at {from}, so it is enlarged in the {to} image.
history.combine.upscaledMany: {n} images have a lower scale, so they are enlarged in the {to} image.
history.combine.tooLarge: At {scale} the image would pass 16,384 px on a side, so it is made at 1x.
history.combine.tooLargeAt1x: Even at 1x the image passes 16,384 px on a side, so it cannot be opened. You can pick fewer images or try another layout.
history.combine.skipped: {name} was left out, because only screenshots can be combined.
history.combine.skippedMany: {n} of the selected captures were left out, because only screenshots can be combined.
history.col.name: Name
history.inspector.label: Details
history.inspector.title: Details
history.inspector.name: Name
history.link.title: Link
history.link.uploadedWithDeletion: Uploaded {when}, and the deletion handle is saved.
history.link.notUploaded: This capture lives only on this Mac.
history.link.notUploaded@other: This capture lives only on this computer.
history.text.title: Recognised text
history.text.pending: The text of this capture is being read.
history.text.failed: The text of this capture could not be read.
history.text.none: No text was found in this capture.
history.text.readHere: The text was read on this Mac.
history.text.readHere@other: The text was read on this computer.
history.text.recordingNote: Search skips recordings, because their text is not recognised.

history.delete.title: Delete this capture?
history.delete.lead: “{name}” leaves the history, and the choices below decide what else goes.
history.delete.leadMany: The {n} captures leave the history, and the choices below decide what else goes.
history.delete.fileChoice: Move the file to the Trash
history.delete.fileChoice@windows: Move the file to the Recycle Bin
history.delete.fileChoice@linux: Move the file to the trash
history.delete.fileChoiceMany: Move their {n} files to the Trash
history.delete.fileChoiceMany@windows: Move their {n} files to the Recycle Bin
history.delete.fileChoiceMany@linux: Move their {n} files to the trash
history.delete.fileHelpMany: Only the files you saved go to the Trash, where they stay until it is emptied.
history.delete.fileHelpMany@windows: Only the files you saved go to the Recycle Bin, where they stay until it is emptied.
history.delete.fileHelpMany@linux: Only the files you saved go to the trash, where they stay until it is emptied.
history.delete.hostHelp: Everyone who has the link loses access, and this cannot be undone.
history.delete.hostLocked: Allow uploads is off in Settings › General, and Glimpsfy deletes nothing on {host} until you turn it back on.
history.delete.hostLockedOffline: Work offline is on in Settings › General, and Glimpsfy deletes nothing on {host} until you turn it off.
history.delete.linkLost: The entry holds the only link and deletion key Glimpsfy has for this copy, so after the delete it can no longer remove the copy.
history.delete.many.linkLost: The entries hold the only links and deletion keys Glimpsfy has for these copies, so after the delete it can no longer remove them.
history.delete.both: The entry, the file and the hosted copy are removed, and the file waits in the Trash until it is emptied.
history.delete.both@windows: The entry, the file and the hosted copy are removed, and the file waits in the Recycle Bin until it is emptied.
history.delete.both@linux: The entry, the file and the hosted copy are removed, and the file waits in the trash until it is emptied.
history.delete.fileOnly: The file goes to the Trash, while the copy on {host} stays online and its link keeps working.
history.delete.fileOnly@windows: The file goes to the Recycle Bin, while the copy on {host} stays online and its link keeps working.
history.delete.fileOnly@linux: The file goes to the trash, while the copy on {host} stays online and its link keeps working.
history.delete.hostOnly: The file stays in its folder, and the copy on {host} is deleted for everyone.
history.delete.none: Only the history entry is removed, and both the file and the link keep working.
history.delete.file: The entry leaves the history, and the file waits in the Trash until it is emptied.
history.delete.file@windows: The entry leaves the history, and the file waits in the Recycle Bin until it is emptied.
history.delete.file@linux: The entry leaves the history, and the file waits in the trash until it is emptied.
history.delete.keepFile: Only the history entry is removed, and the file stays in its folder.
history.delete.ownAndHost: The capture is removed from this Mac, and the copy on {host} is deleted for everyone.
history.delete.ownAndHost@other: The capture is removed from this computer, and the copy on {host} is deleted for everyone.
history.delete.ownKeepHost: The capture is removed from this Mac, while the copy on {host} stays online and its link keeps working.
history.delete.ownKeepHost@other: The capture is removed from this computer, while the copy on {host} stays online and its link keeps working.
history.delete.own: This capture exists only in the history, so deleting it removes it from this Mac.
history.delete.own@other: This capture exists only in the history, so deleting it removes it from this computer.
history.delete.many.both: The {n} entries, their saved files and their copies on {host} are removed, and the files wait in the Trash.
history.delete.many.both@windows: The {n} entries, their saved files and their copies on {host} are removed, and the files wait in the Recycle Bin.
history.delete.many.both@linux: The {n} entries, their saved files and their copies on {host} are removed, and the files wait in the trash.
history.delete.many.file: The {n} entries leave the history, and their saved files wait in the Trash until it is emptied.

history.delete.many.host@other: The {n} captures are removed from this computer, and their copies on {host} are deleted for everyone.
history.delete.many.hostKeepFile: The saved files stay in their folders, and the copies on {host} are deleted for everyone.

history.delete.many.own@other: These {n} captures exist only in the history, so deleting them removes them from this computer.

history.toast.copiedImage: The image is ready to paste.
history.toast.trashed: The saved files went to the Trash.
history.toast.trashed@windows: The saved files went to the Recycle Bin.
history.toast.trashed@linux: The saved files went to the trash.
history.toast.hostedDeletedOne: Deleted the copy on the host.
history.toast.exportSkipped: {n} could not be copied, because their files are missing.

history.inspector.linkOnly: Only the link was kept, because this capture was uploaded without being copied or saved.

history.onPage.deleteTextOne: {host} deletes uploads only on its own page, which is now open in your browser. Delete the upload there first, then finish deleting the capture here; until then it keeps its link.
history.onPage.deleteText: {host} deletes uploads only on its own pages, which are now open in your browser. Delete the uploads there first, then finish deleting the {n} captures here; until then they keep their links.
history.toast.linkForgotten: Removed the link from the capture.
record.record.pickWindow: Click a window to record it.
record.countdown.label: Recording starts in {n}
record.mode.label: What to record
record.system.unavailable: This Mac cannot record system audio.
record.system.unavailable@other: This computer cannot record system audio.
record.mic.notRecorded: The microphone was off when this take started.
record.perm.mic.label: Microphone access
record.perm.mic.title: Glimpsfy cannot hear your microphone.
record.perm.mic.text: macOS blocks the microphone until you allow Glimpsfy under Privacy & Security › Microphone. The meter starts moving as soon as access is on.
record.perm.mic.text@windows: Windows blocks the microphone until you allow desktop apps under Privacy & security › Microphone in Settings. The meter starts moving as soon as access is on.
record.perm.camera.label: Camera access
record.perm.camera.title: Glimpsfy cannot see your camera.
record.perm.camera.text: macOS blocks the camera until you allow Glimpsfy under Privacy & Security › Camera. The bubble shows the picture as soon as access is on.
record.options.persist: These choices stay for the next recording.
record.options.limitHelp: The recording stops and saves itself at {time}.
record.options.limitDisk: A recording of {time} writes about {need}, and the disk has {free} free. The recording stops when the disk fills.
record.discard.question: Discard this recording?
record.bubble.label: Camera bubble
record.trim.title: Trim recording
record.trim.discardTip: Move the recording to the Trash
record.trim.discardTip@windows: Move the recording to the Recycle Bin
record.trim.discardTip@linux: Move the recording to the trash
record.trim.trashTitle: Move this recording to the Trash?
record.trim.trashTitle@windows: Move this recording to the Recycle Bin?
record.trim.trashTitle@linux: Move this recording to the trash?
record.trim.trashText: The recording moves to the Trash, and Finder can put it back from there. Files you already exported stay where they are.
record.trim.trashText@windows: The recording moves to the Recycle Bin, and you can restore it from there. Files you already exported stay where they are.
record.trim.trashText@linux: The recording moves to the trash, and you can restore it from there. Files you already exported stay where they are.
record.trim.playFailed: The preview cannot play this file. Export still works.
record.trim.diskFull: The take stopped on its own because the disk is almost full.
record.trim.emptyText: When you record the screen, the take opens here so you can trim and export it.
record.transcript.label: Text
record.transcript.title: Text
record.transcript.langNote: If the text makes no sense, choose the spoken language, and Glimpsfy reads the recording again in that language.
record.transcript.promptText: To cut by the text, Glimpsfy downloads the speech model once. The model is {size} and then runs on this Mac, so the recording never leaves this Mac.
record.transcript.promptText@other: To cut by the text, Glimpsfy downloads the speech model once. The model is {size} and then runs on this computer, so the recording never leaves this computer.
record.transcript.afterDownload: When it ends, the recording turns into text on its own.
record.transcript.downloadFailed: The model could not be downloaded. Check the connection, then try again.
record.transcript.unavailable: This build cannot turn speech into text yet, so the text stays empty.
record.transcript.transcribingText: The recording is read on this Mac, and the text appears here as it is written.
record.transcript.transcribingText@other: The recording is read on this computer, and the text appears here as it is written.
record.transcript.failed: The speech could not be turned into text. Try again, and restart Glimpsfy if it keeps happening.
record.transcript.busy: Glimpsfy is already turning another recording into text. Try again when it ends.
record.transcript.stopped: The reading stopped before the end. Start it again to get the whole text.
record.transcript.noAudioText: The recording was made without the microphone and without system audio, so it holds no speech to turn into text.
record.transcript.noSpeechTitle: No speech is heard in the recording
record.transcript.noSpeechText: No speech was heard, so there is no text to cut. You can still shorten the quiet parts, which Glimpsfy finds from the sound level.
record.export.label: Export
record.export.title: Export
record.export.gifSilent: GIF files carry no sound, so the voice-over only travels in an MP4.
record.export.gifLarge: Many chat apps reject GIFs over 10 MB, so a smaller width or frame rate is safer.
record.export.leftSeconds: About {n} seconds are left. The export keeps running if you close this window.
record.export.leftMinutes: About {n} minutes are left. The export keeps running if you close this window.
record.export.running: The export keeps running if you close this window.
record.upload.noProvider: No upload host is chosen yet. Choose one in Settings › Upload, then upload again.
record.upload.blocked: {problem} Fix it in Settings › Upload, then upload again.
record.upload.sending: Glimpsfy is sending the file to {name} ({percent}).
record.error.setup.permission_denied: macOS does not let Glimpsfy record the screen yet. Allow it under Privacy & Security › Screen & System Audio Recording, then press Record again.
record.error.setup.permission_denied@oth: The system did not let Glimpsfy record the screen. Allow it when the system asks, then press Record again.
record.error.setup.not_found: The display or window to record is gone. Choose another one and press Record again.
record.error.setup.invalid_argument: Glimpsfy cannot record this target as it is. Choose another target or a larger area, then press Record again.
record.error.export.not_found: The recording is no longer on disk, so it cannot be exported.
record.error.export.invalid_argument: These export settings do not fit this recording. Change them and try again.
record.error.export.io: The file could not be written. Check that the disk has room and that the folder still exists, then try again.
record.error.upload.permission_denied: This host is not confirmed yet, so nothing was sent. Upload again to confirm it.
record.error.upload.invalid_argument: A setting of the upload host is not valid. Fix it in Settings › Upload.
record.error.upload.provider: The upload host refused the file. Check it in Settings › Upload, then try again.
record.error.upload.not_found: The exported file disappeared before it could be sent. Upload again.
record.error.trash.not_found: The recording is no longer on disk, so nothing moved to the Trash.
record.error.trash.not_found@windows: The recording is no longer on disk, so nothing moved to the Recycle Bin.
record.error.trash.not_found@linux: The recording is no longer on disk, so nothing moved to the trash.
record.error.trash.io: The recording could not be moved to the Trash. Check the disk, then try again.
record.error.trash.io@windows: The recording could not be moved to the Recycle Bin. Check the disk, then try again.
record.error.trash.io@linux: The recording could not be moved to the trash. Check the disk, then try again.
record.error.permission_denied: macOS does not allow this yet. Allow Glimpsfy under System Settings › Privacy & Security, then try again.
record.error.permission_denied@other: The system does not allow this yet. Allow Glimpsfy in its privacy settings, then try again.
record.error.busy: Another recording or export is running. Wait until it ends, then try again.
record.error.io: A file could not be read or written. Check the disk, then try again.
record.error.capture: The screen could not be recorded. Try again, and restart Glimpsfy if it keeps happening.
record.error.not_implemented: This part of recording is not ready yet in this version.
record.error.not_found: Something this needs is gone, such as a display, a window or a device. Try again.
record.error.invalid_argument: Glimpsfy could not use that choice. Try again.
record.error.other: Something went wrong. Try again, and restart Glimpsfy if it keeps happening.
settings.title: Settings
settings.common.offlineNote: Work offline is on, so this stays off.
settings.error.notImplemented: This build of Glimpsfy cannot do that yet, so nothing changed.
settings.error.permission: macOS refused the permission, so allow Glimpsfy in System Settings and try again.
settings.error.permission@other: The system refused the permission, so allow Glimpsfy in its privacy settings and try again.
settings.error.io: Glimpsfy could not read or write a file ({detail}), so check the folder and try again.
settings.error.invalid: Glimpsfy refused the value ({detail}), so correct it and try again.
settings.error.notFound: Glimpsfy could not find it ({detail}), so choose it again.
settings.error.provider: The host answered “{detail}”, so check its settings and try again.
settings.error.keychain: The keychain refused access ({detail}), so unlock it and try again.
settings.error.keychain@windows: Windows Credential Manager refused access ({detail}), so try again, and restart Glimpsfy if it keeps refusing.
settings.error.keychain@linux: The desktop keyring refused access or is missing ({detail}), so unlock it, or install GNOME Keyring or KWallet, and try again.
settings.error.other: Something went wrong ({detail}), so try again.
settings.error.login: macOS refused to add Glimpsfy to the login items, so the switch stayed off. Allow Glimpsfy in Login Items and turn the switch on again.
settings.error.login@windows: Windows refused to add Glimpsfy to the startup apps, so the switch stayed off. Allow Glimpsfy under Startup apps and turn the switch on again.
settings.error.login@linux: Glimpsfy could not add itself to the apps that start at login, so the switch stayed off. Check that your home folder can be written to, then turn the switch on again.
settings.folder.missing: The folder does not exist now, so Glimpsfy makes it at the next save.
settings.folder.readOnly: Glimpsfy may not write in this folder, so saving fails until you choose another one.
settings.general.startAtLoginHelp: Glimpsfy opens no window at start and waits in the menu bar.
settings.general.startAtLoginHelp@window: Glimpsfy opens no window at start and waits in the notification area.
settings.general.startAtLoginHelp@linux: Glimpsfy opens no window at start and waits in the tray.
settings.general.showIcon: Show the icon in the menu bar
settings.general.showIcon@windows: Show the icon in the notification area
settings.general.showIcon@linux: Show the icon in the tray
settings.general.showIconHelp: When the icon is hidden, open Glimpsfy again from Applications to reach these settings.
settings.general.showIconHelp@windows: When the icon is hidden, open Glimpsfy again from the Start menu to reach these settings.
settings.general.showIconHelp@linux: When the icon is hidden, open Glimpsfy again from your applications to reach these settings.
settings.general.delayHelp: A delay leaves time to open a menu before the capture.
settings.general.allowUploadsHelp: When this is off, Glimpsfy hides the upload buttons and sends nothing to an upload host.
settings.general.offlineHelp: While this is on, Glimpsfy opens no network connection at all.
settings.general.checkUpdatesHelp: Glimpsfy will look at its GitHub releases once a day and install nothing until you confirm.
settings.general.privacy: Glimpsfy has no account and sends no telemetry. It goes online only to upload, to download a recognition or speech model or to check for updates, and Work offline turns all of that off.
settings.shortcuts.recordScreenHelp: The key that starts a recording also stops it.
settings.shortcuts.listening: Press the new keys, or press Esc to keep the old ones.
settings.shortcuts.needsModifier: Add ⌘, ⌥ or ⌃, so the key keeps typing in other apps.
settings.shortcuts.needsModifier@windows: Add Ctrl, Alt or the Windows key, so the key keeps typing in other apps.
settings.shortcuts.needsModifier@linux: Add Ctrl, Alt or Super, so the key keeps typing in other apps.
settings.shortcuts.commandAlone: Apps use ⌘ with one key for their own commands, so add ⇧, ⌥ or ⌃.
settings.shortcuts.commandAlone@other: Apps use Ctrl with one key for their own commands, so add Shift or Alt.
settings.shortcuts.refusedBySystem: macOS did not accept {keys}, perhaps because another app holds it, so record other keys.
settings.shortcuts.refusedBySystem@windo: Windows did not accept {keys}, perhaps because another app holds it, so record other keys.
settings.shortcuts.refusedBySystem@linux: The desktop did not accept {keys}, perhaps because another app holds it, so record other keys.
settings.shortcuts.systemFallback: macOS uses {keys} for a shortcut of its own.
settings.shortcuts.systemFallback@window: Windows uses {keys} for a shortcut of its own.
settings.shortcuts.systemFallback@linux: The desktop uses {keys} for a shortcut of its own.
settings.shortcuts.commands.title: Commands for your desktop
settings.shortcuts.commands.desc: Your desktop gives apps no global shortcuts, so bind these commands to keys in its keyboard settings, and each one runs its action in Glimpsfy.
settings.shortcuts.cleared: {other} kept {keys}, so this action has no shortcut now.
settings.shortcuts.restoreHelp: Restoring the defaults replaces every shortcut you changed.
settings.shortcuts.overlayDesc: These keys work while the capture tools are open, and they stay fixed.
settings.shortcuts.overlay.removeSize: Delete a saved size (in the size menu)
settings.shortcuts.system.screenFile: macOS uses ⇧⌘3 to save a picture of the screen.
settings.shortcuts.system.areaFile: macOS uses ⇧⌘4 for its own area screenshot.
settings.shortcuts.system.toolbar: macOS uses ⇧⌘5 to open its screenshot toolbar.
settings.shortcuts.system.touchBar: macOS uses ⇧⌘6 to save a picture of the Touch Bar.
settings.shortcuts.system.screenCopy: macOS uses ⌃⇧⌘3 to copy a picture of the screen.
settings.shortcuts.system.areaCopy: macOS uses ⌃⇧⌘4 to copy a picture of an area.
settings.shortcuts.system.finderSearch: macOS uses ⌥⌘Space to open a Finder search.
settings.shortcuts.system.inputSource: macOS uses ⌃Space to switch the input source.
settings.shortcuts.system.characterViewe: macOS uses ⌃⌘Space to open the Character Viewer.
settings.shortcuts.system.lockScreen: macOS uses ⌃⌘Q to lock the screen.
settings.shortcuts.system.dock: macOS uses ⌥⌘D to show and hide the Dock.
settings.shortcuts.system.win.lock: Windows uses Win+L to lock the computer.
settings.shortcuts.system.win.desktop: Windows uses Win+D to show the desktop.
settings.shortcuts.system.win.close: Windows uses Alt+F4 to close the active window.
settings.shortcuts.system.win.printScree: Windows opens its own screen capture with Print Screen until you turn that off under Accessibility › Keyboard in Settings.
settings.shortcuts.system.win.snip: Windows uses Win+Shift+S to open the Snipping Tool.
settings.shortcuts.system.win.screenFile: Windows uses Win+Print Screen to save a picture of the screen.
settings.shortcuts.system.linux.printScr: Most desktops use Print Screen for their own screenshot tool.
settings.shortcuts.system.linux.lock: Many desktops use Super+L to lock the screen.
settings.shortcuts.system.linux.close: Most desktops use Alt+F4 to close the active window.
settings.recorder.ariaEmpty: {name} has no shortcut. Press to record one.
settings.output.name: File name
settings.output.nameHelp: Saving never replaces a file; a counter is added to the name instead.
settings.output.templateEmpty: The file name needs at least one character.
settings.output.templateCharacter: A file name cannot contain “{character}”, so use a dash instead.
settings.output.formatPng: PNG keeps every pixel, which suits text and interface captures.
settings.output.formatJpeg: JPEG suits photos, and it cannot keep transparency.
settings.output.formatWebp: WebP keeps every pixel like PNG, and its files are smaller.
settings.output.optimisePngHelp: Glimpsfy compresses each saved PNG again before it writes the file, so a save can take a few seconds longer and no pixel changes.
settings.output.retinaHelp: At 1× the width and height are halved, so the file matches the size you saw.
settings.output.copyAfterSave: Copy to the clipboard after saving
settings.output.send.head: Send to app
settings.output.send.help: The Send list shows these apps in this order, and the digits are its shortcuts. Glimpsfy brings the app forward and presses ⌘V, and it never presses Return. A recording always goes as a file.
settings.output.send.granted: Granted. Glimpsfy can press ⌘V in the target app for you.
settings.output.send.denied: Not granted. Glimpsfy brings the app forward and puts the capture on the clipboard, and you press ⌘V.
settings.output.send.pathNote: It gets the file’s path instead of the image.
settings.output.send.closedNote: If it is closed, it is opened first.
settings.output.send.missing: It was not found on this Mac.
settings.output.send.empty: No app has been added yet. The apps you add here appear in the Send list.
settings.output.backgroundHelp: It fills the space around the corners and the shadow, and JPEG always uses white.
settings.output.keepHelp: Older entries leave the history, and files in your save folder stay where they are.
settings.output.keepHelpTrash: Older entries leave the history, and their files in your save folder go to the Trash.
settings.output.keepHelpTrash@windows: Older entries leave the history, and their files in your save folder go to the Recycle Bin.
settings.output.keepHelpTrash@linux: Older entries leave the history, and their files in your save folder go to the trash.
settings.output.trashSaved: Move saved files to the Trash too
settings.output.trashSaved@windows: Move saved files to the Recycle Bin too
settings.output.trashSaved@linux: Move saved files to the trash too
settings.output.trashSavedHelp: A file that goes to the Trash can still be put back from there.
settings.output.trashSavedHelp@windows: A file that goes to the Recycle Bin can still be put back from there.
settings.output.trashSavedHelp@linux: A file that goes to the trash can still be put back from there.
settings.output.spaceUnavailable: This build cannot measure the history yet.
settings.output.spaceEmpty: Zero KB · the history is empty
settings.output.clearText: This deletes {count} captures from this Mac and frees {size}. Pinned captures, files in your save folder and links you uploaded stay where they are.
settings.output.clearText@other: This deletes {count} captures from this computer and frees {size}. Pinned captures, files in your save folder and links you uploaded stay where they are.
settings.output.clearTextOne: This deletes 1 capture from this Mac and frees {size}. Pinned captures, files in your save folder and links you uploaded stay where they are.
settings.output.clearTextOne@other: This deletes 1 capture from this computer and frees {size}. Pinned captures, files in your save folder and links you uploaded stay where they are.
settings.output.clearTextUnknown: This deletes every capture that is not pinned from this Mac. Files in your save folder and links you uploaded stay where they are.
settings.output.clearTextUnknown@other: This deletes every capture that is not pinned from this computer. Files in your save folder and links you uploaded stay where they are.
settings.output.clearedNote: The history was cleared, and {size} became free.
settings.recording.videoDesc: Recordings are MP4 files encoded by the hardware of this Mac.
settings.recording.videoDesc@other: Recordings are MP4 files encoded by the hardware of this computer.
settings.recording.codecHelp: HEVC files are about half the size, and a few older apps cannot play them.
settings.recording.resolutionHelp: Half resolution keeps long recordings small.
settings.recording.systemAudioMissing: This Mac cannot record system audio, so recordings stay without it.
settings.recording.systemAudioMissing@ot: This computer cannot record system audio, so recordings stay without it.
settings.recording.deviceGoneHelp: The saved device is not connected now, so the system default is used until it returns.
settings.recording.devicesUnavailable: This build cannot list devices yet, so the system default is used.
settings.recording.noMicrophones: No microphone is connected, so recordings have no voice.
settings.recording.noCameras: No camera is connected, so recordings show no webcam.
settings.recording.separateTracks: Keep each source on its own track
settings.recording.separateTracksHelp: A mixed track is added as well, so the file still plays everywhere.
settings.recording.keysHelp: The keys appear in a small bar on the recording.
settings.recording.keysOnlyHelp: Only keys pressed with ⌘, ⌥ or ⌃ appear, so typed text and passwords stay out of the video.
settings.recording.keysOnlyHelp@other: Only keys pressed with Ctrl, Alt or the system key appear, so typed text and passwords stay out of the video.
settings.recording.webcamDesc: The recording bar turns the camera on, and these rows shape its bubble.
settings.recording.cornerHint: You can drag the bubble to another corner before the recording starts.
settings.recording.gifDesc: The export view starts with these values.
settings.recording.speechModelDesc: The trim window turns speech into text with this model, so a recording can be cut by its words. The model downloads once and then runs on this Mac, and neither the recording nor its text leaves this Mac.
settings.recording.speechModelDesc@other: The trim window turns speech into text with this model, so a recording can be cut by its words. The model downloads once and then runs on this computer, and neither the recording nor its text leaves this computer.
settings.recording.speechModelLoading: Glimpsfy is reading the state of the model.
settings.recording.speechModelMissing: This build cannot turn speech into text yet, so the model cannot be downloaded.
settings.ocr.visionHelp: Vision is built into macOS, runs on the Neural Engine and needs no download.
settings.ocr.windowsOcrHelp: Text recognition is built into Windows and reads the languages whose pack includes it.
settings.ocr.systemEngineHelp: The system's own engine reads the text without a download.
settings.ocr.ppOcrHelp: The open PP-OCR models run on this Mac after a one-time download for each script.
settings.ocr.ppOcrHelp@other: The open PP-OCR models run on this computer after a one-time download for each script.
settings.ocr.ppOcrMissing: PP-OCR is not part of this build yet, so it cannot be chosen.
settings.ocr.modelsDesc: Each model downloads once and then works offline.
settings.ocr.modelsMissing: This build cannot download PP-OCR models yet, because the PP-OCR engine is not part of it.
settings.ocr.modelsNeeded: PP-OCR reads text only once its models are downloaded, so download the models for your languages below.
settings.ocr.modelsLoading: Glimpsfy is reading the list of models.
settings.ocr.modelsNone: This build lists no PP-OCR models.
settings.ocr.languagesHelp: With detection on, the ticked languages win when a text could be either. The list comes from the engine.
settings.ocr.languagesDownload: {n} more languages need a download that this build cannot make yet.
settings.ocr.languagesLoading: Glimpsfy is asking the engine for its languages.
settings.ocr.languagesUnavailable: This engine cannot list its languages in this build yet.
settings.ocr.languagesEmpty: The engine lists no languages on this Mac.
settings.ocr.languagesEmpty@other: The engine lists no languages on this computer.
settings.ocr.lineBreaksHelp: When this is off, the lines of a paragraph are joined into one.
settings.ocr.codesHelp: A link inside a code appears as an action next to the selection.
settings.ocr.privacy: Recognition runs on this Mac, and no image or text is sent anywhere.
settings.ocr.privacy@other: Recognition runs on this computer, and no image or text is sent anywhere.
settings.upload.hostsDesc: Glimpsfy uploads only when you ask, and it asks before the first upload to each host.
settings.upload.pickDesc: Each host opens its own page with its terms and settings.
settings.upload.copyHelp: Markdown copies ![](link), which GitHub shows as an image.
settings.upload.openInBrowser: Open the link in the browser
settings.upload.emptyText: Pick a host below to turn on uploads. Until you do, nothing leaves this Mac.
settings.upload.emptyText@other: Pick a host below to turn on uploads. Until you do, nothing leaves this computer.
settings.upload.noHostsText: This build offers no upload host, so nothing leaves this Mac.
settings.upload.noHostsText@other: This build offers no upload host, so nothing leaves this computer.
settings.upload.loadFailedTitle: The hosts could not be listed
settings.upload.testHelp: The test asks the host whether it accepts these settings.
settings.upload.offNote: Uploads are off in General, so Glimpsfy sends nothing to these hosts.
settings.upload.offlineNote: Work offline is on in General, so Glimpsfy sends nothing to these hosts.
settings.upload.testRefused: {name} refused the test, so check its answer and the settings above.
settings.upload.testFix: Correct the fields marked in red, and test again.
settings.upload.notConfirmed: Glimpsfy asks before the first upload to {name}.
settings.upload.secretKept: The value is now in the macOS Keychain, and the field stays empty so nobody can read it.
settings.upload.secretKept@windows: The value is now in the Windows Credential Manager, and the field stays empty so nobody can read it.
settings.upload.secretKept@linux: The value is now in the desktop keyring, and the field stays empty so nobody can read it.
settings.upload.secretRemoved: The value was removed from the Keychain.

settings.upload.secretRemoved@linux: The value was removed from the keyring.
settings.upload.secretStored: Paste a new value to replace the stored one
settings.upload.pairDuplicate: The name {name} is already in the list, so pick another one.
settings.upload.pairsHelp: The values are kept in the macOS Keychain.
settings.upload.pairsHelp@windows: The values are kept in the Windows Credential Manager.
settings.upload.pairsHelp@linux: The values are kept in the desktop keyring.
settings.upload.pairsKept: The values you typed are now in the macOS Keychain.
settings.upload.pairsKept@windows: The values you typed are now in the Windows Credential Manager.
settings.upload.pairsKept@linux: The values you typed are now in the desktop keyring.
settings.upload.confirmedFor: You confirmed uploads to {destination}, so Glimpsfy no longer asks first.
settings.upload.notConfirmedFor: Glimpsfy asks before the first upload to {destination}.
settings.upload.importHelp: A ShareX .sxcu file fills in the form below, and its header, parameter and argument values go to the keychain.
settings.upload.importHelp@windows: A ShareX .sxcu file fills in the form below, and its header, parameter and argument values go to the Credential Manager.
settings.upload.importHelp@linux: A ShareX .sxcu file fills in the form below, and its header, parameter and argument values go to the keyring.
settings.upload.pairsMissing: Some names have no value in the keychain yet, so type their values again.
settings.upload.pairsMissing@windows: Some names have no value in the Credential Manager yet, so type their values again.
settings.upload.pairsMissing@linux: Some names have no value in the keyring yet, so type their values again.
settings.upload.secretOnFile: A value is stored in the macOS keychain, and Glimpsfy never shows it again.
settings.upload.secretOnFile@windows: A value is stored in the Windows Credential Manager, and Glimpsfy never shows it again.
settings.upload.secretOnFile@linux: A value is stored in the desktop keyring, and Glimpsfy never shows it again.
settings.upload.testBlocked: The test can run once the settings marked above are complete.
settings.about.licence: Glimpsfy is free software under the MIT licence.
settings.about.welcomeHelp: It shows the permissions and the first steps again.
settings.about.welcomeHelp@linux: It shows the first steps again.
settings.about.ackDesc: Glimpsfy is built on these projects, and each keeps its own licence.
settings.about.ijg: This software is based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.
popover.capture.label: Capture
popover.delay.label: Delay
popover.interval.title: Interval capture
popover.interval.summary: The series lasts about {duration} and is saved in the {folder} folder. The history shows it as one entry.
popover.interval.summaryManual: The series lasts until you stop it, at most 12 hours, and is saved in the {folder} folder. The history shows it as one entry.
popover.interval.areaFirst: You select the area first, and the series starts once you finish it.
popover.interval.skippedWhy.one: The system's capture service was busy for the frame at {time}; the series goes on, and the history shows this frame as a gap.
popover.interval.skippedWhy.many: The system's capture service was last busy for the frame at {time}; the series goes on, and the history shows the skipped frames as gaps.
popover.interval.waiting: The first frame is on its way.
popover.interval.noHistory: The history is off, so the frames go straight into {folder}.
popover.recent.unavailable: Recent captures are not available yet.
popover.recent.failed: Glimpsfy could not read the history.
popover.hint: Drag a thumbnail into any app to drop it as a file.
popover.empty.title: Your last five captures appear here.
popover.empty.keys: Press {keys} and drag across the screen to take the first one.
popover.empty.noKeys: Choose Capture area and drag across the screen to take the first one.
popover.act.copied: The capture is on the clipboard.
popover.act.linkCopied: The link is on the clipboard.
popover.perm.title: Screen recording is off
popover.perm.body: Glimpsfy cannot capture the screen until you allow it again in System Settings.
popover.perm.restartBody: macOS applies the permission only after Glimpsfy restarts.
pin.collapsed: Double-click the tile to restore the pin.
pin.loadFailed: Glimpsfy could not load the pinned image.
firstrun.welcome.title: Welcome to Glimpsfy
firstrun.welcome.lead: Glimpsfy needs one permission to capture your screen. The other two are optional, and you can allow them later in Settings.
firstrun.welcome.lead@windows: Glimpsfy needs no permission to capture your screen on Windows. The microphone is optional, and you can allow it later in Settings.
firstrun.welcome.lead@linux: Glimpsfy needs no permission to capture your screen on this desktop, so you can go straight to your shortcut.
firstrun.welcome.leadWayland: Your desktop asks you to share the screen the first time you take a capture, and Glimpsfy asks for nothing before that.
firstrun.perm.screenRecording.name: Screen Recording
firstrun.perm.screenRecording.why: Glimpsfy needs this permission to capture anything on your screen.
firstrun.perm.microphone.name: Microphone
firstrun.perm.microphone.why: Glimpsfy uses the microphone only when you add your voice to a recording.
firstrun.perm.accessibility.name: Accessibility
firstrun.perm.accessibility.why: Glimpsfy uses this permission to snap the selection to window edges and to show your keystrokes in recordings.
firstrun.wait: Turn on the switch next to Glimpsfy in the list that just opened. Glimpsfy notices the change by itself.
firstrun.wait@windows: Turn on access for Glimpsfy, or for desktop apps, on the page that just opened. Glimpsfy notices the change by itself.
firstrun.restartWhy: macOS applies this permission only after Glimpsfy restarts, and this window opens again at the same step.
firstrun.privacy.title: What stays on this Mac
firstrun.privacy.account: Glimpsfy has no account and sends no usage data.
firstrun.privacy.upload: A capture leaves this Mac only when you upload it, and the first upload to each service asks you first.
firstrun.privacy.upload@other: A capture leaves this computer only when you upload it, and the first upload to each service asks you first.
firstrun.privacy.ocr: Text recognition runs on this Mac.
firstrun.privacy.ocr@other: Text recognition runs on this computer.
firstrun.privacy.screen: This permission lets an app see the whole screen at any time, and Glimpsfy reads it only after you start a capture.
firstrun.privacy.screen@other: Glimpsfy reads the screen only after you start a capture, and never in the background.
firstrun.privacy.source: The source code is public, so anyone can check these sentences.
firstrun.hint.ok: You can allow the optional ones later in Settings.
firstrun.hint.none: Nothing here needs your permission, so you can continue.
firstrun.fin.title: Choose your capture shortcut
firstrun.fin.lead: You will press it many times a day, so pick keys that your hand finds without looking.
firstrun.fin.leadCommand: Your desktop gives apps no global shortcuts, so you bind the command below to keys in its keyboard settings.
firstrun.fin.oursHelp: The macOS screenshot keys keep working next to Glimpsfy.
firstrun.fin.oursHelp@windows: Print Screen keeps opening the Windows screen capture next to Glimpsfy.
firstrun.fin.oursHelp@linux: The desktop’s own screenshot keys keep working next to Glimpsfy.
firstrun.fin.replaceHelp: Glimpsfy opens Keyboard Shortcuts so you can turn the macOS ones off.
firstrun.fin.replaceHelp@windows: Glimpsfy opens the keyboard page of Windows Settings so you can give Print Screen to Glimpsfy.
firstrun.fin.replaceHelp@linux: Your desktop may keep Print Screen for its own screenshot tool, and you turn that off in its keyboard settings.
firstrun.fin.replaceSteps: Glimpsfy takes these keys for Capture area when you press Done. macOS keeps them until you turn off “Save picture of selected area as a file” under Keyboard Shortcuts › Screenshots, and Glimpsfy never changes that setting for you.
firstrun.fin.replaceSteps@windows: Glimpsfy takes Print Screen for Capture area when you press Done. Windows opens its own screen capture with the key until you turn off “Use the Print screen key to open screen capture” under Accessibility › Keyboard, and Glimpsfy never changes that setting for you.
firstrun.fin.replaceSteps@linux: Glimpsfy takes Print Screen for Capture area when you press Done. A desktop that keeps the key for its own screenshot tool refuses it, so turn that shortcut off in the desktop’s keyboard settings first, and Glimpsfy never changes them for you.
firstrun.fin.loginHelp: Glimpsfy waits in the menu bar and opens no window.
firstrun.fin.loginHelp@windows: Glimpsfy waits in the notification area and opens no window.
firstrun.fin.loginHelp@linux: Glimpsfy waits in the tray and opens no window.
firstrun.fin.loginRefused: macOS did not add Glimpsfy to the login items. You can allow it in System Settings under General › Login Items.
firstrun.fin.loginRefused@windows: Windows did not add Glimpsfy to the startup apps. You can allow it in Settings under Apps › Startup.
firstrun.fin.loginRefused@linux: Glimpsfy could not add itself to the apps that start at login. Check that your home folder can be written to, then try again.
firstrun.fin.tryKeys: Press {keys} and drag across anything on the screen to take your first capture.
firstrun.fin.tryNoKeys: Choose Capture area in the menu bar and drag across anything on the screen to take your first capture.
firstrun.fin.tryNoKeys@windows: Choose Capture area from Glimpsfy’s icon in the notification area and drag across anything on the screen to take your first capture.
firstrun.fin.tryNoKeys@linux: Choose Capture area in the menu of Glimpsfy’s tray icon and drag across anything on the screen to take your first capture.
firstrun.fin.tryCommand: Once the keys are bound, press them and drag across anything on the screen; until then, choose Capture area in the tray menu.
firstrun.fin.saveFailed: Glimpsfy could not save your choice.
firstrun.fin.keysRefused: Glimpsfy could not take {keys}. Turn the macOS keys off first, or keep the Glimpsfy keys.
firstrun.fin.keysRefused@windows: Glimpsfy could not take {keys}. Turn off the Windows screen capture key first, or keep the Glimpsfy keys.
firstrun.fin.keysRefused@linux: Glimpsfy could not take {keys}, because the desktop holds it. Turn the desktop’s screenshot shortcut off first, or keep the Glimpsfy keys.
firstrun.fin.keysTaken: Glimpsfy could not take {keys}, because {other} already uses them. Give {other} other keys in Settings › Shortcuts, or keep the Glimpsfy keys.
toast.savedFallback: {folder} could not be reached, so the capture went here instead.
toast.reason.io: Glimpsfy could not read or write the file.
toast.reason.not_found: The file is no longer there.
toast.reason.capture: macOS could not capture the screen.
toast.reason.capture@other: The system could not capture the screen.
toast.reason.invalid_argument: Glimpsfy could not use what it was given.
toast.fix.permission_denied: Allow Glimpsfy under Screen & System Audio Recording in System Settings, then try again.
toast.fix.permission_denied@windows: Allow Glimpsfy under Privacy & security in Windows Settings, then try again.
toast.fix.permission_denied@linux: Share the screen when the desktop asks, then try again.
toast.fix.io: Check that the save folder exists and has free space, then try again.
toast.fix.not_found: Take the capture again, or choose another file.
toast.fix.busy: Finish or close the open capture, then try again.
toast.fix.provider: Check the host in Settings › Upload, then try again.
toast.fix.other: Try again, and restart Glimpsfy if it keeps failing.
toast.diskFull: The disk is almost full, so the recording stopped.
toast.diskFullSaved: Everything recorded until then is saved in {folder}.
toast.series.diskFull: The disk is full, so the interval capture stopped.
toast.series.stalled: The system's capture service did not answer for {n} frames in a row.
toast.series.windowGone: The window the series followed was closed.
toast.series.permission: Glimpsfy lost the screen recording permission, so it took no more frames.
toast.pathCopied: The file’s path was copied as text.
toast.pathTemporary: History is off, so this temporary file is deleted after 24 hours.
toast.send.openingBody: It is pasted once the window is ready.
toast.send.noPermissionBody: Glimpsfy needs Accessibility permission to press ⌘V. The capture is ready on the clipboard, so press ⌘V yourself for now.
toast.send.timedOutBody: Nothing was pasted, and the capture is still on the clipboard.
toast.send.failedBody: The capture is still on the clipboard, so you can switch to the app and press ⌘V.
toast.timeUp: Time is up, so the recording stopped and was saved.
tray.needsXwayland: Glimpsfy needs XWayland to capture this Wayland session. Turn XWayland on in your desktop's settings, or log in to an X11 session.
update.status.off: This copy does not update itself, because it was not installed from a release.
update.status.offline: Glimpsfy could not reach GitHub, so it tries again later.
update.status.checking: Glimpsfy is looking for a new version.
update.status.ready: Version {version} is downloaded and installs when Glimpsfy restarts.
update.status.available: Version {version} is out, but this copy cannot replace itself, so download it from the releases page.
update.status.installing: Glimpsfy is installing the update and restarts in a moment.
update.status.failedDownload: The download of version {version} failed, so Glimpsfy tries again later.
update.status.failedSignature: The download of version {version} did not match its signature, so Glimpsfy discarded it.
update.status.failedInstall: Version {version} could not be installed, so Glimpsfy keeps running this version.
update.ready.title: Glimpsfy {version} is ready
update.ready.body: The update installs when Glimpsfy restarts, which takes a few seconds.
beautify.title: Beautify
beautify.windowNote: The window’s own corner and shadow are used.
beautify.name: Preset name
beautify.jpeg: JPEG cannot keep transparency, so the padding and the area around the corners are saved white.
beautify.pngChosen: This capture is saved as PNG.
beautify.missing: “{name}” was not found. This capture uses the preset’s gradient.
beautify.failed: The preset could not be saved.
settings.beautify.auto: Apply a preset to every capture
settings.beautify.autoHelp: F skips the preset for that capture only.
settings.beautify.jpeg: Because the output format is JPEG, a transparent background and the area around rounded corners are saved white.
settings.beautify.valuesHelp: A preset’s values change in the Beautify panel of a capture, with Update preset.
settings.agents.serverDesc: Agents ask Glimpsfy for a screenshot of a window, the screen or an area, or for the text in an area, and every request waits for your approval.
settings.agents.enableHelp: The server accepts connections only from processes on this Mac and never opens to the network.
settings.agents.notListening: The server could not open, so agents cannot connect.
settings.agents.commandHelp: Claude Code, Cursor and Zed start the server with this command.
settings.agents.connectedDesc: A timed permission lasts at most 10 minutes and ends when the screen locks.
settings.agents.off: The server is off, so no agent can connect and no request comes in.
settings.agents.none: No agent has connected yet. Once you add the command to an agent's settings, the agent shows up here.
settings.agents.logDesc: The log keeps every request with its answer for 7 days.
settings.agents.logEmpty: No agent sent a request in the last 7 days.
settings.agents.note: A screenshot or text you approve goes only to the requesting agent's process on this Mac. Whether the agent sends it on to a language model depends on the agent's own settings, so connect only agents you trust.
